info.desc: Californication is the seventh studio album by American alternative rock band Red Hot Chili Peppers, released on June 8, 1999 on Warner Bros. Records. Produced by Rick Rubin, Californication marked the return of John Frusciante, who had previously appeared on Mother's Milk and Blood Sugar Sex Magik, to replace Dave Navarro as the band's guitarist. Frusciante's return was credited with changing the band's sound altogether. The record was a notable shift in style from what was produced with Navarro. podcast.body: Many albums by the Red Hot Chili Peppers, including "Californication," are cited as examples of recordings that can be "unlistable" on CD due to excessive compression from the "loudness wars." Conversely, uncompressed vinyl versions of these albums allow the subtleties of the performance and recording to be preserved and heard. "I find many Red Hot Chili Peppers albums unlistable on CD because of that overcompressure, because of those loudness wars."

podcast.body: Released in 1999, this album is frequently cited as one of the worst-sounding records affected by the "loudness wars" due to excessive compression during mastering. The heavy compression resulted in audible clipping, distortion, and a near-zero dynamic range, leading to a comparatively unsatisfactory listening experience. An unauthorized "Unmastered Edition" circulates online, offering a superior sonic experience with enhanced clarity in Chad Smith's cymbals, subtle keyboard lines, improved background vocals by Flea, greater separation in Flea's bass notes, and more openness in John Frusciante's chords. "There is so much compression used in the mastering that you can hear all kinds of clipping and distortion."

It was an even bigger hit than "Blood Sugar Sex Magik," selling almost 20 million copies worldwide and winning a Grammy, solidifying Frusciante's crucial role in the band's sound. "The California Cation album released on June 8th, 1999, was an even bigger hit than blood sugar sex magic, selling almost 20 million copies around the planet, along with winning a Grammy."
